# Open the prefilled Start run popup when an agent calls `open_start_run` (web)

## What to build

When an agent in a graph-manager terminal calls the `open_start_run` tool, the server queues a request; this slice makes the browser act on it. The overview poll (every 2 s) also fetches `GET /api/agent-requests`. A new `AgentRequestHost`, mounted once for the whole app, handles each pending request:

- if the Terminals page currently shows the request's terminal in a visible pane, it acks the request (`POST /api/agent-requests/:id/ack`) and opens the **Start run** drawer right there, prefilled with the request's workspace, tasks folder, spec, and (when given) provider and run options;
- otherwise it shows a toast once per request: `<Agent label> in <repo> wants to start a run` (`An agent in <repo> …` when the agent is unknown) with **Open**, which acks and opens the same prefilled drawer in place (no navigation).

A request that is still pending when the user later opens the Terminals page with that terminal visible pops up then. `StartRunDrawer` gains a `prefill` prop that wins over the workspace's saved run defaults.

Server side already in the codebase (read it): `GET /api/agent-requests` → `{ requests: AgentRequest[] }` and `POST /api/agent-requests/:id/ack` → 204 / 404, in `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/agent-requests.ts`; the shape is in `apps/graph-manager/src/server/agent-requests.ts`:
```ts
interface AgentRequest { id: string; kind: "start-run"; terminalId: string; workspaceId: string; agent?: string; terminalTitle?: string; createdAt: string;
  prefill: { tasksDir: string; spec: string; provider?: string; options?: RunOptionsBody } }
```
`TerminalInfo.agent` and `AgentInfo` (`{ id, label, installed, connect }`) exist in `web/types.ts`, and the Terminals page fetches `GET /api/agents`. The spec is `docs/prd/agent-tools.md` (Decisions about the popup; "Web" section).

## Context: files to read before implementing

- `docs/prd/agent-tools.md` — the contract.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/overview.tsx` (whole file: `Overview` interface lines 10–25, `EMPTY`, `poll()` lines 61–110 with `Promise.allSettled`) — add `agentRequests` to the poll and the context.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/App.tsx` (lines 62–78) — mount `AgentRequestHost` inside `OverviewProvider` (and inside `BrowserRouter`), e.g. next to `<Shell>`.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/main.tsx` — `ToastProvider` wraps `App`, so `useToast()` works in the host.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/ui/toast.tsx` (lines 5–40) — `ToastAction` supports `onClick` (use it instead of `to`), `TOAST_MS` = 6 s.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/StartRunDrawer.tsx` (lines 64–155: props, the open/workspace effects, and the run-defaults effect that sets `provider`, `tasksDir`, `spec`, `form` from `/api/workspaces/:ws/run-defaults`; `formOf(options)` from `../runOptions`) — add `prefill`.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/runOptions.ts` — `formOf`, `RunOptionsBody`, `emptyForm`.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/Terminals.tsx` (lines 145–147 `shown`; lines 173–180 `paneBadges`: the map of terminal ids visible in panes) — publish the visible terminal ids.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/Runs.tsx` (line 479) — how the drawer is mounted today (`<StartRunDrawer open onClose workspaces initialWorkspace />`); Runs keeps its own instance.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/StartRunDrawer.test.tsx` and `pages/Terminals.test.tsx` (lines 1–120) — test patterns (fetch mock via `vi.stubGlobal("fetch", …)`, providers, `MemoryRouter`).

## Patterns to follow

**Types** (`web/types.ts`): add
```ts
/** `GET /api/agent-requests` (src/server/agent-requests.ts). */
export interface AgentRequest { id: string; kind: "start-run"; terminalId: string; workspaceId: string; agent?: string; terminalTitle?: string; createdAt: string;
  prefill: { tasksDir: string; spec: string; provider?: string; options?: Record<string, unknown> } }
```

**Overview**: add `agentRequests: AgentRequest[]` to `Overview`/`EMPTY`, a fifth request `api<{ requests: AgentRequest[] }>("/api/agent-requests")` in the `allSettled` list, kept like the others (last good answer on failure). Keep `allFailed` meaning "every request failed" (include the new one). Existing overview tests mock fetch by URL; make sure an unmocked `/api/agent-requests` (a 404 or thrown error in older tests) does not break them — it just keeps `[]`.

**Visible terminals context** (`web/agentRequests.tsx`, new):
```tsx
/** Terminal ids shown in a visible pane of the Terminals page; empty on other pages. */
const VisibleTerminals = createContext<{ ids: ReadonlySet<string>; set(ids: ReadonlySet<string>): void } | null>(null);
export function VisibleTerminalsProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode })
export function useSetVisibleTerminals(ids: ReadonlySet<string>): void // effect: set on change, clear (empty set) on unmount
```
In `Terminals.tsx`: `useSetVisibleTerminals(useMemo(() => new Set(paneBadges.keys()), [paneBadges]))`. Mount `VisibleTerminalsProvider` in `App.tsx` around `Shell` and the host. Make the hook a no-op without the provider (tests render `Terminals` without it).

**Host** (same file):
```tsx
export function AgentRequestHost(): JSX.Element
```
- reads `useOverview()` (`agentRequests`, `workspaces`, `terminals`), the visible ids, and `useToast()`.
- keeps `toasted = useRef(new Set<string>())` and `opened = useRef(new Set<string>())`.
- effect on `[agentRequests, visible]`: for each request not in `opened`: if `visible.has(r.terminalId)` and `!document.hidden` → `openFor(r)`; else if not in `toasted` → add, and `toast.show({ tone: "live", text, action: { label: "Open", onClick: () => openFor(r) } })`.
- `openFor(r)`: add to `opened`, `void post(\`/api/agent-requests/${encodeURIComponent(r.id)}/ack\`).catch(() => {})`, set the drawer state `{ workspaceId, prefill }`.
- toast text: agent label from `{ claude: "Claude Code", codex: "Codex", opencode: "OpenCode", qwen: "Qwen Code" }[r.agent]` else `An agent`; repo = the workspace id's last `~` segment (`github~octo~hello` → `hello`): `Claude Code in hello wants to start a run`.
- renders `<StartRunDrawer open={!!drawer} onClose={() => setDrawer(undefined)} workspaces={overview.workspaces} initialWorkspace={drawer?.workspaceId} prefill={drawer?.prefill} />`.
- GOTCHA: `post` is in `web/api.ts`; check its signature (`post(url, body?, method?)`).

**Drawer prefill** (`StartRunDrawer.tsx`): new optional prop
```ts
prefill?: { tasksDir: string; spec: string; provider?: string; options?: unknown }
```
In the run-defaults effect (the one depending on `[open, ws]`), after the defaults answer (or the fallback) is applied, if `prefill` is set **and** `ws === initialWorkspace`, apply: `setTasksDir(prefill.tasksDir)`, `setSpec(prefill.spec)`, `provider` when it is one of `PROVIDERS`, and `setForm(formOf(prefill.options))` when `options` is given (otherwise keep the defaults' form). Add `prefill` to that effect's deps, or keep it in a ref, so it applies on each open. Without `prefill` nothing changes (existing tests must pass unchanged).

## Step-by-step tasks

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/web/types.ts` — `AgentRequest`.
### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/web/overview.tsx` — poll `/api/agent-requests`, expose `agentRequests`.
### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/web/agentRequests.tsx` — provider, hook, host.
### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/web/App.tsx` — mount `VisibleTerminalsProvider` and `<AgentRequestHost />`.
### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/Terminals.tsx` — `useSetVisibleTerminals`.
### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/StartRunDrawer.tsx` — `prefill`.

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/web/agentRequests.test.tsx`
- **IMPLEMENT** (`// @vitest-environment jsdom`, fetch mock like Terminals.test.tsx answering `/api/runs`, `/api/terminals`, `/api/workspaces`, `/api/forges`, `/api/agent-requests`, the ack POST, and the drawer's `/api/workspaces/:ws/run-defaults` (`{}`), `/inspect`, `/settings`, `/api/sandbox/status`):
  - a request for terminal `t2` while a test component sets visible ids `{t2}` (render `<ToastProvider><OverviewProvider><VisibleTerminalsProvider><SetVisible ids={["t2"]} /><AgentRequestHost/></…>` in a `MemoryRouter`) → the `start-run-drawer` opens, `start-run-tasks` input has `.agents/tasks/agent-tools` and the spec input has `docs/prd/agent-tools.md`, and one POST `/api/agent-requests/<id>/ack` was sent.
  - prefill `provider: "fake"`, `options: { concurrency: 3 }` → the provider control and concurrency field show those values (find the testids in `StartRunDrawer.tsx` / `RunOptionsFields.tsx`).
  - same request with no visible terminal → no drawer; a toast `Claude Code in hello wants to start a run`; clicking **Open** opens the prefilled drawer and acks.
  - the toast is shown only once across several polls (advance timers or call `refresh()` twice).
- Add one case to `pages/StartRunDrawer.test.tsx`: `prefill` wins over the saved run defaults for the same workspace.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With the calling terminal visible on the Terminals page, a queued request opens the Start run drawer prefilled (tasks folder, spec, provider/options when given) within one poll, and acks it.
- [ ] Elsewhere, the request shows a single toast `<Agent> in <repo> wants to start a run` with **Open**, which opens the prefilled drawer and acks it.
- [ ] Clicking **Start run** in the prefilled drawer posts `/api/runs/<ws>` with those values (existing submit code).
- [ ] Existing overview, Terminals, Runs and StartRunDrawer tests pass.
- [ ] Tests pass: `npm test -w graph-manager -- src/web`.
- [ ] Look at it yourself (TESTING.md "graph-manager"): open a terminal in a workspace with committed `diamond/` + `spec.md` fixtures, then from inside that terminal call the tool directly with `curl -s -X POST -H "authorization: Bearer $GM_INTERNAL_TOKEN" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "{\"terminalId\":\"$GM_TERMINAL_ID\",\"cwd\":\"$PWD\",\"input\":{\"tasksDir\":\"diamond\",\"spec\":\"spec.md\"}}" $GM_INTERNAL_URL/api/internal/tools/open_start_run` and check the popup opens next to the terminal.

## Validation commands

```bash
npm run build -w graph-execution && npm run build -w graph-manager
npm run typecheck && npm run lint
npm test -w graph-manager -- src/web
```
